name: OpenAI
products: ChatGPT, GPT-4o, DALL·E 3, Sora, Whisper, Codex, API Platform
investors: Microsoft ($13B), Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, a16z
desc: Leading AI lab building general-purpose artificial intelligence. ChatGPT has 200M+ weekly active users and transformed the AI industry.
key_metrics: 200M+ weekly active users; GPT-4o multimodal; Enterprise 4x YoY; $80B valuation
pros: Market leader in AI; ChatGPT is a household name; Microsoft partnership; Fastest growing tech product ever; Strong developer ecosystem
cons: Massive losses ($5B+); Safety concerns; Key talent departures; Transition from nonprofit to for-profit controversial; Heavy dependence on Microsoft
history: 2015: Founded as nonprofit by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, others. 2019: Shifted to 'capped profit'. 2020: GPT-3 launched. 2022: ChatGPT launched (fastest growing app ever). 2023: GPT-4 launched; Sam Altman briefly fired then reinstated. 2024: GPT-4o, Sora, $80B valuation.
competitors: Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta AI, Mistral AI, xAI
current_situation: Dominant AI company but burning cash rapidly. Converting to for-profit structure. Key employees leaving to start competitors. ChatGPT growth stabilizing but enterprise revenue accelerating.

name: Anthropic
products: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus, Claude API, Constitutional AI
desc: AI safety company founded by ex-OpenAI researchers. Creator of Claude AI, focused on building safe, beneficial AI using constitutional AI approach.
key_metrics: Claude 3.5 Sonnet tops benchmarks; Amazon $4B; AI safety pioneer
pros: Top-tier AI models (Claude 3.5); Strong safety culture; Amazon and Google backing; Best coding AI; Trusted by enterprises
cons: Burning cash ($2B loss); Smaller than OpenAI; Less brand recognition; Heavy reliance on cloud partners; Slower product launches
history: 2021: Founded by Dario & Daniela Amodei (ex-OpenAI VP). 2023: Claude 1 launched; Google invested $2B; Amazon invested $4B. 2024: Claude 3 family launched; Claude 3.5 Sonnet becomes top coding model.
competitors: OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta AI, Mistral AI, Cohere
current_situation: Strong #2 position in AI. Claude 3.5 Sonnet widely praised for coding. Enterprise revenue growing rapidly. Positioning as the 'safe AI' alternative to OpenAI.

name: Google DeepMind
products: Gemini AI, AlphaFold, AlphaGo, Veo, Imagen 3, SynthID, Genie
desc: World's leading AI research lab. AlphaFold solved protein folding (Nobel Prize 2024). Built AlphaGo that defeated world champion. Now building Gemini AI models powering Google products.
key_metrics: Nobel Prize 2024; AlphaFold 200M+ proteins; Gemini 1.5 Pro; Powering Google Search
pros: Groundbreaking research (AlphaFold, AlphaGo); Unlimited Google funding; Nobel Prize; Gemini models competitive; World's best AI researchers
cons: Slow to productize research; Internal Google politics; Lost early LLM lead to OpenAI; Gemini launch was rocky; Brain drain to startups
history: 2010: Founded as DeepMind Technologies. 2014: Acquired by Google for $500M. 2016: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol. 2020: AlphaFold solves protein folding. 2023: Merged with Google Brain to form Google DeepMind. 2024: Demis Hassabis wins Nobel Prize.
competitors: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta AI, Microsoft Research
current_situation: Merged Google Brain and DeepMind teams. Gemini models powering Google products. Nobel Prize 2024 for AlphaFold. Strong position but competing with Google's own product teams.

name: Mistral AI
products: Mistral Large 2, Mixtral 8x22B, Codestral, Le Chat, La Plateforme
investors: Microsoft, Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, BPI France
desc: Europe's AI champion. Fastest unicorn in European history. Building open-weight LLMs competing with American AI labs.
key_metrics: Open-weight models; €5.8B in 1 year; EU AI Act compliant
pros: Open-weight models; European AI champion; Rapid growth; EU compliance advantage; Strong technical team from DeepMind/Meta
cons: Small compared to US labs; Limited funding vs OpenAI; Needs to scale; Brand not well known outside tech; Regulatory uncertainty
history: 2023: Founded by ex-DeepMind/Meta researchers. Raised €105M seed (largest in Europe). 2024: Mixtral 8x22B; Mistral Large; €600M Series B; Microsoft partnership.
competitors: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta AI, Aleph Alpha
current_situation: Europe's leading AI company. Strong open-source community support. Growing enterprise customers. Positioned as EU-compliant alternative.

name: xAI
products: Grok 2, Grok-1.5 Vision
investors: Elon Musk, Valor Equity, Vy Capital, Sequoia
desc: Elon Musk's AI company building Grok chatbot. Training on one of the world's largest GPU clusters with 100K NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
key_metrics: 100K H100 GPU cluster; Grok on X platform; $24B valuation
pros: Elon Musk brand; Massive GPU cluster; Access to X (Twitter) data; Real-time information; Huge valuation
cons: Very small team; Late to market; Controversial leadership; X platform declining; No enterprise offering yet
history: 2023: Founded by Elon Musk after leaving OpenAI board. Grok 1 launched on X. 2024: Grok 2 launched; Raised $6B; Building massive GPU supercluster in Memphis.
competitors: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta AI
current_situation: Building rapidly with massive compute. Grok available only through X Premium. Limited market impact so far but massive infrastructure investment.

name: Hugging Face
products: Transformers library, Model Hub, Spaces, Inference API, AutoTrain
desc: The GitHub of machine learning. Open-source platform hosting 500K+ AI models and 100K+ datasets used by every major AI company.
key_metrics: 500K+ models; 100K+ datasets; 50K+ organizations
pros: Essential AI infrastructure; Open-source ecosystem; Used by everyone; Strong community; All major companies as investors
cons: Monetization challenges; Low revenue vs valuation; Competition from cloud providers; Model hosting costs high
history: 2016: Founded as chatbot company. 2018: Pivoted to open-source AI platform. 2021: Raised $40M. 2023: $235M round at $4.5B; Google, Amazon, NVIDIA invested.
competitors: GitHub (for code), AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI
current_situation: De facto standard for sharing AI models. Growing enterprise tier. Every major AI lab publishes models on Hugging Face.

name: Perplexity AI
products: Perplexity Search, Perplexity Pro, Perplexity API, Perplexity Pages
investors: Jeff Bezos, NVIDIA, IVP, NEA, Databricks
desc: AI-powered answer engine challenging Google Search. Provides sourced, real-time answers using AI. Growing rapidly as alternative to traditional search.
key_metrics: 10M+ monthly users; Jeff Bezos backed; Challenging Google
pros: Innovative AI search; Real-time sourced answers; Jeff Bezos backing; Fast growing; Best search alternative
cons: Tiny revenue; Copyright concerns with publishers; Google could crush it; Burning cash; No moat yet
history: 2022: Founded by ex-Google AI researcher. 2023: Series A. 2024: $3B valuation; Jeff Bezos invested; 10M+ users.
competitors: Google Search, Microsoft Bing, You.com, Brave Search
current_situation: Fastest growing search alternative. Publishers pushing back on content scraping. Strong product-market fit but faces Google's AI Overviews competition.

name: Midjourney
products: Midjourney v6, AI image generation via Discord and web
desc: AI image generation company that became profitable with ~50 employees. Known for the highest quality artistic AI image generation. Operates primarily through Discord.
key_metrics: $200M revenue; ~50 employees; Self-funded; Profitable
pros: Profitable with tiny team; Best image quality; No outside investors needed; Strong artist community; $200M revenue
cons: Discord-only (limiting); Copyright lawsuits; Small team limits features; No API; Competition from DALL-E, Stable Diffusion
history: 2021: Founded by David Holz (ex-Leap Motion). 2022: v1-v4 launched on Discord. 2023: v5 with photorealistic quality. 2024: v6 launched; Working on web app.
competitors: OpenAI DALL-E, Stability AI, Adobe Firefly, Google Imagen
current_situation: Most profitable AI company per employee. Building web interface. Facing copyright lawsuits from artists. Quality leadership vs competitors.

name: Stability AI
products: Stable Diffusion 3, Stable Video, Stable Audio, Stable Zero123
desc: Pioneer of open-source generative AI. Stable Diffusion is the most widely-used image generation model, downloaded 30M+ times.
key_metrics: Stable Diffusion 30M+ downloads; Open-source leader
pros: Open-source champion; Most downloaded image model; Covers image/video/audio/3D; Developer community
cons: Massive losses; CEO turnover; Funding challenges; Monetization struggles; Key talent leaving
history: 2019: Founded. 2022: Stable Diffusion launched (viral). 2023: Raised $100M; CEO controversy. 2024: New CEO; Stable Diffusion 3; Financial struggles.
competitors: Midjourney, OpenAI DALL-E, Adobe Firefly, Google Imagen
current_situation: Struggling financially despite product success. New leadership stabilizing. Open-source model but hard to monetize.

name: Cohere
products: Command R+, Embed v3, Rerank 3, Aya (100+ languages)
investors: NVIDIA, Oracle, Salesforce Ventures, Inovia Capital
desc: Enterprise AI company co-founded by Aidan Gomez, co-author of the Transformer paper ('Attention Is All You Need'). Specializes in enterprise RAG and multilingual AI.
key_metrics: Transformer co-author CEO; Enterprise RAG; 100+ languages via Aya
pros: Transformer paper co-author as CEO; Enterprise focus; Multilingual (100+ languages); Strong RAG capabilities; Privacy-first
cons: Smaller than competitors; Low brand awareness; Limited consumer products; Revenue growing slowly
history: 2019: Founded by Aidan Gomez (Transformer co-author). 2022: Series B. 2023: $2.2B valuation; Aya multilingual model. 2024: Command R+ enterprise model.
competitors: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft Azure AI
current_situation: Strong enterprise niche. Aya multilingual model differentiates. Growing but overshadowed by larger competitors.

name: Apple
products: iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch, AirPods, Vision Pro, Apple Silicon, iOS, macOS, Apple Intelligence AI
desc: World's most valuable company. Creator of the iPhone, which revolutionized smartphones. Known for premium design, vertical integration, and an ecosystem of 2.2B active devices.
key_metrics: $3.4T market cap; 2.2B active devices; Services $85B+; #1 smartphone brand
pros: World's most valuable company; Unmatched brand loyalty; Services growing $85B+; Apple Silicon dominates; Vision Pro innovative; Massive cash reserves
cons: iPhone growth slowing; China market challenges; EU regulatory pressure (DMA); AI behind competitors; High prices limit accessibility; Antitrust scrutiny
history: 1976: Founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak in garage. 1984: Macintosh. 1997: Jobs returns, saves Apple. 2001: iPod. 2007: iPhone revolutionizes phones. 2010: iPad. 2011: Jobs passes away. 2014: Apple Watch. 2020: Apple Silicon M1. 2023: Vision Pro announced. 2024: Apple Intelligence AI.
competitors: Samsung, Google (Android), Microsoft, Huawei, Xiaomi
current_situation: $3.4T market cap but iPhone growth plateauing. Apple Intelligence AI playing catch-up. EU forcing App Store changes. Services revenue is bright spot. Vision Pro struggling in market.

name: Microsoft
products: Windows, Azure, Microsoft 365, GitHub, LinkedIn, Teams, Copilot AI, Xbox, VS Code, Bing
desc: Enterprise and cloud computing giant. Azure is #2 cloud platform. Invested $13B in OpenAI. Copilot AI integrated across all products. GitHub hosts 100M+ developers.
key_metrics: Azure growing 29% YoY; GitHub 100M+ devs; $13B OpenAI; LinkedIn 1B+ members
pros: Azure #2 cloud and growing; Copilot AI in everything; OpenAI partnership; GitHub dominance; Diversified revenue; Strong enterprise relationships
cons: Antitrust risks; OpenAI dependence for AI strategy; Gaming division underperforming; Search market share still tiny; High valuation
history: 1975: Founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. 1985: Windows launched. 1995: Windows 95 + Internet Explorer. 2000: .NET. 2001: Xbox. 2014: Satya Nadella becomes CEO (transformation). 2016: LinkedIn acquired ($26B). 2018: GitHub acquired ($7.5B). 2023: $13B invested in OpenAI; Copilot launched.
competitors: Google (Cloud), Amazon (AWS), Apple, Salesforce
current_situation: In the best position in decades under Nadella. AI-first strategy with Copilot everywhere. Azure challenging AWS. But OpenAI relationship complex and AI monetization unproven.

name: Google / Alphabet
products: Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Gmail, Maps, Google Cloud, Gemini AI, Pixel, Waymo
desc: Dominates internet with 92% search market share. YouTube has 2.5B users. Android powers 72% of smartphones. Building Gemini AI models.
key_metrics: 92% search share; YouTube 2.5B users; Android 72% mobile; Cloud $33B
pros: Search monopoly (92%); YouTube dominance; Android ecosystem; Google Cloud growing fast; DeepMind world-class research; Waymo autonomous driving leader
cons: Over-reliance on ads (80% revenue); AI search threatens ad model; Antitrust lawsuits (lost DOJ case); Gemini launch was rocky; Cloud #3 behind AWS/Azure
history: 1998: Founded by Larry Page, Sergey Brin at Stanford. 2004: IPO. 2006: YouTube acquired ($1.65B). 2008: Android launched. 2014: DeepMind acquired. 2015: Restructured as Alphabet. 2023: Bard/Gemini launched. 2024: Lost DOJ antitrust case.
competitors: Microsoft (Bing/Azure), Amazon (AWS), OpenAI, Meta, Apple
current_situation: Dominant but existentially threatened by AI disrupting search ads. Lost DOJ antitrust case. Gemini AI improving but behind ChatGPT in consumer perception. Cloud growing well.

name: Amazon
products: Amazon.com, AWS Cloud, Prime Video, Alexa, Ring, Kindle, Whole Foods, MGM, Amazon Go
desc: World's largest e-commerce and cloud platform. AWS powers 32% of cloud market. 200M+ Prime subscribers. 1.5M employees making it one of world's largest employers.
key_metrics: AWS 32% cloud share; 200M+ Prime; 1.5M employees; Logistics rivals UPS
pros: AWS market leader; E-commerce dominance; Prime ecosystem lock-in; Unmatched logistics network; Diversified business
cons: Thin retail margins; Antitrust scrutiny; Labor practices criticism; Alexa losing billions; High valuation; AI behind competitors
history: 1994: Founded by Jeff Bezos as online bookstore. 2006: AWS launched. 2007: Kindle. 2014: Alexa/Echo. 2017: Whole Foods acquired ($13.7B). 2021: Andy Jassy becomes CEO. 2023: Invested $4B in Anthropic.
competitors: Walmart (retail), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Shopify, Alibaba
current_situation: AWS growth slowing but still dominant. E-commerce facing Shein/Temu competition. Invested $4B in Anthropic for AI. Prime Video gaining content. Logistics network is hidden moat.

name: Meta
products: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, Threads, Llama AI, Quest VR, Ray-Ban Meta
desc: Social media empire reaching 3.98B monthly users. Open-sourced Llama AI models. Investing $16B/year in Reality Labs (VR/AR).
key_metrics: 3.98B monthly users; Instagram 2B; Llama 3 open-source; $16B/year Reality Labs
pros: 3.98B users unmatched; Instagram cash cow; Llama AI open-source leader; Reels competing with TikTok; Strong ad revenue recovery
cons: $16B/year Reality Labs burn; Metaverse unclear ROI; Youth losing interest in Facebook; Privacy scandals; TikTok competition
history: 2004: Facebook founded by Zuckerberg at Harvard. 2012: IPO + Instagram acquired ($1B). 2014: WhatsApp acquired ($19B). 2021: Renamed to Meta. 2022: Stock crashed 65%. 2023: Threads launched; Llama 2 open-sourced; Stock recovered 200%.
competitors: TikTok/ByteDance, Google/YouTube, Snapchat, X (Twitter), OpenAI
current_situation: Massive comeback story — stock up 200% from 2022 lows. Llama 3 makes Meta an AI leader. Reels competing well with TikTok. Reality Labs still burning cash but Quest 3 shows promise.

name: NVIDIA
products: H100, H200, B200 Blackwell GPUs, CUDA, DGX systems, Omniverse, NVIDIA Drive, GeForce RTX
desc: The engine of the AI revolution. Makes GPUs that train every major AI model. Data center revenue grew 409% in one year. Third most valuable company globally.
key_metrics: 80%+ AI chip share; Data center +409% YoY; Powers ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude; $3T market cap
pros: 80%+ AI training market; CUDA ecosystem moat; Incredible margins (60%+); Every AI company is customer; Jensen Huang visionary leadership
cons: Extreme valuation; Customer concentration risk; AMD/custom chips competition; Cyclical chip industry; Export restrictions to China
history: 1993: Founded by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, Curtis Priem. 1999: Invented GPU. 2006: CUDA launched (key moat). 2012: GPUs used for deep learning. 2023: AI boom sends stock up 300%. 2024: Blackwell architecture; $3T market cap.
competitors: AMD, Intel, Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia, Qualcomm
current_situation: Essentially has monopoly on AI training hardware. Supply-constrained — customers waiting months for chips. Blackwell next-gen launching. But extreme valuation priced for perfection.

name: Tesla
products: Model S/3/X/Y, Cybertruck, Semi, Powerwall, Megapack, Solar Roof, FSD, Optimus Robot, Dojo chip
desc: World's most valuable automaker. Vertically integrated: cars, batteries, solar, AI chips. Pioneering autonomous driving with Full Self-Driving. Developing Optimus humanoid robot.
key_metrics: 1.8M vehicles (2023); 50K+ Superchargers; FSD Beta; Optimus robot
pros: EV market leader; Supercharger network becoming standard; FSD data advantage; Vertically integrated; Brand power; Energy business growing
cons: Elon Musk controversy; Competition intensifying (BYD); Margin pressure; FSD not truly autonomous; Quality concerns; Overvalued vs traditional auto
history: 2003: Founded by Martin Eberhard. 2008: Roadster launched; Elon Musk becomes CEO. 2012: Model S. 2017: Model 3 mass market. 2020: Stock surged 700%; S&P 500. 2023: Cybertruck. 2024: Robotaxi announced.
competitors: BYD, Rivian, Lucid, Toyota, VW, Mercedes EQ, Ford, GM
current_situation: EV competition intensifying, especially from BYD in China. Margins declining. FSD progress but not yet fully autonomous. Energy storage (Megapack) growing rapidly. Optimus robot long-term bet.

name: Samsung
products: Galaxy smartphones, DRAM/NAND memory chips, OLED displays, TVs, home appliances, semiconductor foundry
desc: World's largest memory chip maker and smartphone manufacturer by volume. Produces DRAM, NAND, OLED displays. Major foundry challenging TSMC.
key_metrics: #1 DRAM/NAND; 270M+ phones/year; HBM for AI; Foundry growing
pros: Memory chip dominance; Diversified (chips to appliances); Galaxy brand strong; OLED display leader; HBM chips for AI demand
cons: Founder in legal troubles; Foundry behind TSMC; Chinese competition in phones; Cyclical chip business; Complex conglomerate structure
history: 1938: Founded as trading company. 1969: Samsung Electronics. 1990s: Became DRAM leader. 2009: Galaxy smartphone line. 2016: Note 7 battery crisis. 2017: Founder sentenced to prison. 2024: HBM chips for AI boom.
competitors: TSMC (foundry), SK Hynix (memory), Apple (phones), Micron (memory), LG (displays)
current_situation: Benefiting from AI boom via HBM memory chips. Smartphone competition intense from Apple and Chinese brands. Foundry gap vs TSMC narrowing. Memory prices recovering.

name: TSMC
products: Advanced chip manufacturing: 3nm, 5nm, 7nm process nodes, CoWoS advanced packaging
desc: World's most critical technology company. Makes chips for Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm. Only company manufacturing at 3nm scale. Geopolitically vital as 54% of global foundry market.
key_metrics: 54% global foundry share; Only 3nm at scale; Makes all Apple/NVIDIA chips
pros: Absolute technology leader (3nm); 54% foundry share; Irreplaceable for Apple/NVIDIA; Best margins in industry; Geopolitical importance ensures government support
cons: Taiwan geopolitical risk (China); Customer concentration (Apple ~25%); Capital intensive; Arizona fab delays; Earthquake vulnerability
history: 1987: Founded by Morris Chang. 1990s-2000s: Became leading foundry. 2020: 5nm mass production. 2022: 3nm launched; Arizona fab announced. 2024: NVIDIA/AI demand explosion.
competitors: Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries
current_situation: Indispensable to global tech. AI demand driving record orders. Arizona fab under construction. Taiwan geopolitical tensions remain key risk.

name: TCS

key_metrics: 600K employees; 46 countries; 1000+ clients; BFSI largest vertical; $7.6B pipeline
pros: India's #1 IT company; Massive scale (600K employees); Consistent margins; Low debt; Strong client relationships; Tata brand trust
cons: Revenue concentration in US/EU; Wage inflation in India; AI could disrupt outsourcing model; Slower growth than smaller peers; Attrition challenges
history: 1968: Founded as division of Tata Sons. 1980s: Began US operations. 2004: IPO (India's largest at the time). 2018: Crossed $100B market cap. 2023: $28B revenue; Focus on AI and cloud.
competitors: Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Accenture, Cognizant, IBM
current_situation: Steady growth but AI disruption looms. Investing in generative AI capabilities. Strong deal pipeline at $7.6B. Attrition declining. Digital services now majority of revenue.

key_metrics: 317K employees; Topaz AI platform; 1700+ clients; Finacle powers 500+ banks; Founded with $250
pros: Strong brand and governance; Topaz AI platform; Finacle banking product; Lower attrition than peers; Good margins; NYSE listed

competitors: TCS, Wipro, HCLTech, Accenture, Cognizant, IBM

pros: Diversified across sectors; Strong healthcare vertical; Growing consulting; Azim Premji's philanthropic legacy; Cost efficient

history: 1945: Founded as cooking oil company. 1980s: Azim Premji pivots to IT. 2000: Listed on NYSE. 2019-2024: Multiple CEO changes. 2024: Srini Pallia becomes CEO; AI-first strategy.

pros: Engineering services leader; IBM software products; Strong infrastructure business; Growing faster than Wipro; Low debt

pros: World's largest automaker; Hybrid technology leader; Toyota Production System; Reliability reputation; Diversified globally; Hydrogen bet

name: Salesforce
